chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Housing difficulties in London; his view of people and of Germany
summary: They had trouble getting rooms outside the assigned boarding houses but not in restaurants; Briggs says he does not condemn people, except Hitler, though he loved Germany before.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And we got to London. We heard there were little skirmishes in the East.End. You know where I mean?
Yes.
Well, that's just a quarter. It's a district all by itself, because you have -- it's an international quarter. You have everything more or less.
The seamen of all nations, you know.
Right. It tends to
Briggs
be kind of a slum area, down there, the East End of London.
Yeh, we didn't have any symptoms of any racial dissensions.
Well, while we're on that subject, I know that Armstrong had trouble getting accommodations when he came to Europe.
Yes.
And so did the Mills Brothers.
Yes.
Did you have any problems of that kind when you were in London?
Oh yes, we did. We always had problems, yes.

We only had that problem when we went out -- that is when we quit boarding houses, we tried to get out of boarding houses that were booked for us when we landed, when we arrived. We were all booked in certain boarding houses.
Briggs
But when we tried to get out, to be more or less free, you see, we had quite a lot of difficulties. In getting a hotel room, or --

Hotel room or private rooms. If you find one room, one person finds a room, then you use that person's address for somebody else to try and make a contact to be sure that we're okay, we're bona fide, you know. Well, those are the kinds of things that happened.
Well, what about the restaurants, I mean, were you able to go --
Oh yes, we didn't have no trouble, as far as that's concerned.
No trouble. It was just as far as accommodation?
Accommodations, yes. And I believe, also, that we had
Briggs
a, -- still have a pretty big black colony in London. That is artistic, you see.
Right.
And quite a few of the artists might have been bad fellows.
Yes.
You see. You see, my way of thinking is to find a solution, You see, --
Right.
You see, I'm not going to condemn anyone. There's always two ways to everything.
There must be a reason for something.
Right.
Except one guy. The guy, that this happened in Germany. I mean what he did in Germany, there's no exception for that. As far as I'm concerned, I'm still heartbroken today from it.
Yes, right.
I had a wonderful time
Briggs
in Germany. Germany was simply terrific for me and my orchestra and all the other colored persons that I know. Artists, we had a wonderful time.
Until that guy come in, you see --
